solves: Gathers nph-togglebutton buttons on the same subject in a row, spaced by space/inline, and coordinates their selection, single or multiple, in a toolbar.
use_when: When two or more options on the same subject stay together in the toolbar.
With text, when the icon alone does not say the option; icon only, when the icon is known and each button has a label.
Single selection when the options exclude each other, such as alignment; multiple when they add up, such as bold and italic.
do_not_use_when: For a single option: use nph-togglebutton, without a group.
To join the buttons without space: nph-toggle-group already brings space/inline.
To mix buttons with text and icon-only buttons in the same group: choose one.
Outside a toolbar, in a setting that turns on or off with an immediate effect: use nph-switch.
In a form, when the choice goes with the submission: use nph-checkbox.

label.constraint: The name of the group, the subject, such as Alignment. It becomes the aria-label of the host, which is the role group. A name the consumer puts on the host with aria-label or aria-labelledby also counts. Without any name, the group draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

selection.constraint: single or multiple. It is behavior, not appearance, and the Figma frame leaves it to code; the name and the default are a technical proposal of P76. In single, checking a button unchecks the others and one stays checked once a choice is made; a click on the checked button does nothing. In multiple, each button is free. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

value.type: list of strings (attribute: words separated by spaces)
value.constraint: The checked buttons, by the value attribute of each. The attribute reads value="bold italic"; the property is a list of strings. Single holds zero or one item; a second one is dropped with a warning in development. With no value, none is checked, even if a button carries pressed in the markup: the group writes pressed on every button from it. Setting it from code never fires the event.

slot.constraint: The nph-togglebutton buttons, at least two and with no maximum. Each one names itself with a value attribute, which the group reads and the button ignores: a non-empty word with no whitespace, unique in the group. A button whose value is empty, repeated or has more than one word never joins the selection. A change of the value attribute of a button is picked up by the group. Text, label, icons, disabled and invalid stay on each button.

nph-value-change.constraint: Fired when the person changes the selection. It bubbles, crosses the shadow root and is not cancelable. detail.value is the list of checked values, in the order of the buttons. The nph-change of each button is not stopped.

selection.choose_when: single when the options exclude each other, such as alignment. multiple when they add up, such as bold and italic.

content.choose_when: With text when the icon alone does not say the option. Icon only when the icon is known and each button has a label. The same for every button of the group.
do_not_combine_with: buttons with text and icon-only buttons in the same group: choose one.

group.changes_for_user: The group has no state of its own: it spaces the buttons. Pressed, focus, disabled and invalid belong to each nph-togglebutton.

business_rules: The group is the source of truth of the selection: it writes pressed on every button from value, and the buttons never decide it alone.

In single selection, a click, Enter or Space on the checked button does nothing: it stays checked, no event fires and the click does not reach the page. With no value, none is checked until the first click.
Only a click, Enter or Space by the person fires nph-value-change; setting value from code never fires it.
Changing only the value attribute of a button is enough: the group observes it, writes pressed again and checks the composition, without firing nph-value-change.
There is no maximum number of buttons. With fewer than two buttons the group still renders and warns in development; for a single option use nph-togglebutton.
disabled and invalid stay on each button; the error message of an invalid button stays outside the group.
domain_errors: invalid: a button whose value the screen does not accept shows its own error border; the message is written outside the group.

tokens.color_state_focus: from each nph-togglebutton; the group adds none

ai_hints: Use nph-toggle-group for two or more options on the same subject in a toolbar; for a single option, use nph-togglebutton.
Name the group with label, and every button with a value attribute; an icon-only button also needs its own label.
Choose selection single when the options exclude each other and multiple when they add up.
Read the new value from detail.value of nph-value-change; do not read it from the buttons after a click.
Do not put pressed on a button inside the group: set value on the group.
Use the same content for every button: text on all, or icon only on all.
To fire an action, use nph-button; outside a toolbar use nph-switch; in a form use nph-checkbox.

accessibility.semantics: The host is role group, named by label. Each button is the native button of nph-togglebutton, with aria-pressed. In single selection it is not a radio group: P73 fixes aria-pressed and never aria-checked, so the screen reader reads the state of each button and does not announce that the choice is exclusive. Known limit.
accessibility.accessible_name: The group is named with the subject. Each icon-only button gets its own label, an aria-label on its native button.
keyboard: Tab moves through the buttons, one stop each, in order; a disabled button is skipped.
There are no arrow keys: a roving tabindex across several groups belongs to a toolbar.
accessibility.focus: Each button shows its own focus, as nph-togglebutton does; the group does not receive focus. space/inline is wider than the border and the halo of one button, so the focus of a button is not covered by its neighbor.
accessibility.contrast: Comes from nph-togglebutton: the label and the icon on their own background in both schemes. The group adds no color. The known limit of the focus border of nph-togglebutton, color/primary, holds here unchanged.
accessibility.color_alternative: The pressed button changes its inner area, with background, shadow and outline, not only the text color.

invalid_combinations: No name — no label, no aria-label and no aria-labelledby: the group draws nothing.
A selection that is not single or multiple — the group draws nothing.
A button without value, with a value of more than one word, or two buttons with the same value — the button never joins the selection; the group warns in development.
A value that matches no button — nothing is checked for it; the group warns in development.
More than one value in single — only the first is kept; the group warns in development.
Buttons with text mixed with icon-only buttons — the group renders and warns in development.
A child that is not an nph-togglebutton — it is not part of the selection; the group warns in development.
anti_patterns: Using the group to fire actions.
Mixing buttons with text and icon-only buttons in the same group.
Grouping options that are not on the same subject.
Using the group for a single option.
Using the group outside a toolbar for a setting that turns on or off, where nph-switch is the choice.
Using the group in a form, where nph-checkbox is the choice.
Putting an error message inside the group.

sources.design_md: design.md, space/inline, control/height-default and the core icons align-left, align-center, align-right, bold, italic and underline
sources.decision: P76 — API and semantics of nph-toggle-group
